question: Where can I get mining rights in the United States (exploration permits and mining concessions) as geometry, with holder, commodity, status and dates?

answer.summary: BLM's MLRS publishes 598,739 non-closed mining claims as polygons (ArcGIS REST and bulk CSV/GeoJSON) with case number, claim type and status, but the polygons are built from PLSS legal descriptions, not staked perimeters, and the layer has no holder, commodity or grant dates. Other BLM layers (notices, plans of operations, leases) add commodity, effective/expiry dates (often blank) and a customer-name field. Alaska DNR publishes 123,061 state claim polygons with status only.
main_caveats: BLM claim polygons come from legal land descriptions on the PLSS: two 20.66-acre sample claims map to 396-acre polygons; 45,527 have staff-edited geometry (score 100).
The claims layer has no holder, commodity or grant/expiry date; BLM_PROD is the claim type (lode, placer, mill site, tunnel site), not a mineral.
A claim or permit status ('Active', 'Authorized') shows legal standing only; it does not show that a mine is operating or that minerals exist.
14,997 of 598,739 BLM claim rows have no geometry and 11,821 have no quality score; Closed claims are a separate layer of 79,294 records.
EFF_DT and EXP_DT are blank in most notice, plan and lease records (EXP_DT filled in 760 of 1,252 notices but only 13 of 1,122 plans).
Holder names exist in some BLM layers (CUST_NM_SEC) and in redacted MLRS reports; this card describes availability only and copies no names.
answer.confidence_reason: BLM and Alaska layers were queried and counted; MLRS report contents, other states and the claim-level date fields were not opened.

attributes.note: Polygon per case: 583,742 of 598,739 BLM claims (PLSS-derived; a 20.66-acre claim maps to ~396 acres) and 123,061 Alaska state claims.
attributes.gap_note: BLM says staked boundaries are only in the Notice/Certificate of Location in each case file; the published polygons follow quarter sections, so they are not legal perimeters.

attributes.note: No holder field in the claims layer; CUST_NM_SEC exists in BLM notice, plan and lease layers (e.g. 811 of 1,122 plans). Names are not reproduced here.
attributes.gap_note: MLRS Customer Info reports are redacted for privacy; unredacted ones need a Login.gov account (not created). Alaska's layer points to a separate LAS case-file site.

attributes.note: Claims layer only gives claim type (Lode 502,742; Placer 79,776; Mill Site 15,891); CMMDTY is filled in 1,199 of 1,252 notices and 1,103 of 1,122 plans.
attributes.gap_note: No commodity per mining claim in the layer; claim type is not a mineral, and notices and plans cover far fewer rights than claims.

attributes.note: BLM CSE_DISP (claims: Active 425,853, Filed 166,316, Under Review 6,326); Alaska CS_LABEL ISSUED 41,160, CLOSED 81,863, SUSPEND 33.
EFF_DT, EXP_DT and CSE_DISP_DT exist in permit and lease layers but are sparse (EXP_DT 13 of 1,122 plans); claims and Alaska layers carry no grant or expiry date.
attributes.gap_note: Claims layer only has record Created/Modified stamps; MLRS Case Action(s) reports might hold location and filing dates but were not run (application page only).

how_to_use.example_result: CSE_NR NV105216280, CSE_NAME 'WR 195', BLM_PROD 'Lode Claim', CSE_DISP 'Active', SRC 'LLD', QLTY starting '8:', RCRD_ACRS 20.66; polygon of 27 vertices covering about 396 acres.
steps: Query the FeatureServer with where, outFields and outSR=4326; maxRecordCount is 2000, so page with resultOffset for bulk reads, or use the hub download links.
Filter on CSE_DISP and BLM_PROD for status and claim type; derive the state from the CSE_NR prefix (two letters).
Read the first token of QLTY as the geometry score (0 to 3 direct PLSS match; 4 to 8 calculated; 8.1 to 10 section; 15 partial; 11, 12, 20 no geometry; 100 staff-edited).
For holder, location date and legal descriptions go to the case file or the MLRS reports named by CSE_NR.
reading_traps: The polygon is the legal description mapped to the PLSS, not the staked claim: the two sampled NV claims record 20.66 acres each but their polygons measure about 396 acres.
BLM states it 'only requires that mining claims be identified down to the affected quarter section(s)'.
BLM_PROD is the claim type, not a mineral; there is no commodity or holder column in this layer.

Geometry score counts: 0 to 3 = 378,744; 4 to 8 = 146,235; 8.1 to 10 = 10,787; 15 = 2,449; 11, 12, 20 = 3,171; 100 = 45,527; no score = 11,821. 583,742 rows intersect the US envelope, so about 14,997 have no geometry.
The old gis.blm.gov/nlsdb REST address now redirects to nlsdbpubgis.blm.gov and the service path changed to /arcgishub/rest/services/HUB/.
Created and Modified are epoch milliseconds of record changes, not claim dates.

problems: The earlier gis.blm.gov service path returns HTTP 301 to a root address and 'Service not found'; the working path comes from the data.gov entry. Bulk downloads were checked by headers only (302 then 200).

evidence.claim: Geometry is derived from legal land descriptions, not claim boundaries.
evidence.quote: The BLM only requires that mining claims be identified down to the affected quarter section(s)—as such, that is what the MLRS research map and public reports will reflect, most commonly.

evidence.claim: Staked boundaries are in the case file.
evidence.quote: Claim boundaries, as staked and monumented, are found in the accepted Notice/Certificate of Location as part of the official case file, managed by the BLM State Office having jurisdiction over the claim.
Group 7 – Improved Geometry. Scores of “100” are cases that have had their geometry edited by BLM staff using ArcGIS Pro or MLRS bulk upload tool.

how_to_use.example_result: Non-Energy Leasables sample: CSE_NR CACA106124575, BLM_PROD 'KNOWN LEASING AREA', CSE_DISP 'Authorized', CMMDTY 'Sodium', RCRD_ACRS 35875, EFF_DT and EXP_DT null.
steps: Pick the layer by right type: Locatable_Notices (exploration notices), Locatable_Plans_Of_Operations (BLM_PROD 'Surface Management Plan - Mining' 923, 'Exploration' 183), Non_Energy_Leasables, Coal_Cases (layer id 1), Mineral_Materials.
Query with where, outFields and outSR=4326; use returnCountOnly=true for totals and groupByFieldsForStatistics for distinct values.
Test which of CMMDTY, EFF_DT, EXP_DT and CUST_NM_SEC are filled before relying on them (counts in the reading traps).
reading_traps: Field fill rates: Notices CMMDTY 1,199, EFF_DT 717, EXP_DT 760, CUST_NM_SEC 779 of 1,252; Plans CMMDTY 1,103, EFF_DT 236, EXP_DT 13, CUST_NM_SEC 811 of 1,122; Non-Energy Leasables CMMDTY 6,593, EFF_DT 2,126, EXP_DT 305, CUST_NM_SEC 4,621 of 7,024.
Commodity text is free-ish: 'TWO OR MORE MINERALS' (1,781), 'To Be Defined', 'NONE' and blanks appear.
Notices and plans are surface-management cases for exploration or operations, not the claims themselves; they do not list the claims they cover.
Coal Cases is layer id 1 of its service, not 0.
'Authorized' or 'Pending' says nothing about operation; PRDCNG shows 'Non-Producing' even on authorized plans.
